On March 19, 1920, five months after the ACS formally recognized neurosurgery as a specialty, Cushing hosted 11 surgeons at Peter Bent Brigham Hospital to form the Society of Neurological Surgeons — the first neurosurgical society in the world. Co-founders included Ernest Sachs, Alfred Adson, Charles Frazier, Gilbert Horrax, and Samuel Harvey. Walter Dandy was invited but declined due to strained relationships with Cushing and Frazier. [Verified 2026-03-17 | J Neurosurg 1994 | content_match] The Harvey Cushing Society was organized on October 10, 1931, at the Hotel Raleigh in Washington DC. The first formal meeting was held May 6, 1932 in Boston with 23 charter members, mostly Cushing trainees and younger neurosurgeons. R. Glen Spurling and William P. Van Wagenen were the primary organizers; Cushing hosted the Boston meeting and endorsed the effort. William P. Van Wagenen was elected first president. The society addressed the lack of a venue for younger neurosurgeons excluded from the senior Society of Neurological Surgeons.

[Verified 2026-03-17 | J Neurosurg 2022 | content_match] Penfield founded the Montreal Neurological Institute at McGill University in 1934 with a $1.2 million Rockefeller Foundation grant, serving as its first director until 1960. The MNI was the world's first institute dedicated to integrating neuroscience research with clinical neurosurgery. Penfield mapped the cortical homunculus through intraoperative electrical stimulation of awake patients and developed the Montreal procedure for surgical treatment of epilepsy. The MNI attracted trainees from Hopkins (Dandy's residents) and UCSF (Naffziger's residents), becoming a convergence node for the Halstedian neurosurgical lineage.

[Verified 2026-03-17 | J Neurosurg 2021 | content_match] Naffziger was elected first chairman of the ABNS at its preliminary meeting on November 19, 1939 at the Palmer House in Chicago. The board was officially incorporated in 1940 as the 13th member board of the ABMS. Alfred Adson served as vice-chairman and R. Glen Spurling as secretary-treasurer. The ABNS codified the formal certification of neurosurgeons, requiring dedicated residency training distinct from general surgery.
Bailey returned to Chicago to direct the newly founded institute.

The CNS was the first inclusive neurosurgical society with no membership cap. Arthur Morris, acting upon conversations with Semmes, organized the effort to form the society. Elmer C. Schultz, Semmes' associate at the Semmes-Murphey Clinic since 1948, became the CNS's founding president. The first formal meeting was convened in Memphis in November 1951 — Semmes' home city and sphere of influence. While Semmes did not formally hold office, his inspiration, institutional infrastructure, and trainees were the catalysts for the CNS's creation. Confidence marked moderate because the link is catalytic rather than organizational. 'Fifty years of the Congress of Neurological Surgeons: foundations, objectives, and legacies.' Neurosurgery. 2000 Aug;47(2):261-7. Documents CNS founding context. Note: Semmes' role was indirect — he co-founded the Harvey Cushing Society (1931) with Spurling, Van Wagenen, and Fay. The CNS (1951) emerged from conversations seeded by Semmes' generation. Edge notes already describe this indirect connection.

At its 1967 annual meeting in San Francisco, the Harvey Cushing Society formally changed its name to the American Association of Neurological Surgeons, reflecting its evolution from an intimate collegial club to the primary professional organization for American neurosurgery with over 12,000 members today. [Verified 2026-03-17 | J Neurosurg 2002 | content_match] Howard Christian Naffziger (1884-1961) earned his MD from UC (1909), interned at UCSF, then went to Johns Hopkins in 1912 as assistant resident surgeon under Halsted's program, where he came under the direct mentorship of Harvey Cushing. He became one of Cushing's junior residents alongside Walter Dandy. In 1918, Naffziger served in France with Cushing as part of the Allied Expeditionary Force (WWI). Naffziger was already in the graph with two outgoing edges (→UCSF Dept of Surgery as institutional_founder, →ABNS as society_founder) but had no incoming training edge, making him a disconnected source node in the training lineage. This edge completes the chain: Halsted→Cushing→Naffziger→UCSF, connecting the West Coast surgical establishment to the Hopkins trunk through 3 training generations. The other edges proposed in the T3-01 expansion target (Naffziger→UCSF, Dunphy→UCSF, Debas→ASA) already exist in the graph and are not duplicated here.
